t: The truth about a world reset

b.x: The truth first

There is no single scientific definition of a world reset. There is no exact formula, because this is probability with incomplete data, not a law of physics. What can be done is to use expert estimates and show the arithmetic.
Existential global reset: civilizational collapse at world scale. Irreversible loss of industrial capacity. Death of a large part of the population. A return to pre-industrial societies, or worse.
Regional or partial chaos: collapse or severe instability in regions or countries, without the end of global civilization.
Period: 2026 through 2077. That is 51 years.
The arithmetic
Chance that no disaster happens = (1 − p1) × (1 − p2) × (1 − p3) × … Chance of at least one in 51 years = 1 − that chance.
The chance that none happen is the product of the chances that each one does not happen. Subtract that from 1 to get the chance of at least one.
The close
Some global reset by 2077: 1 − 60% ≈ 40%.
About a 40% chance of a catastrophic global event by 2077. About a 60% chance that none of these six occurs.
Regional chaos and Brazil
This is more likely, because it does not require the whole world to fall. It includes instability, an economic crisis, a severe disaster, a local conflict, and a service that stops in one region.
The largest dangers
Nuclear war or global conflict. About 14%. The risk specialists cite most.
Combined systemic collapse: climate, economy, and society. About 12%. Many consider it the most likely.
Extremely severe climate change. About 10%. The risk grows with time.
A severe pandemic, including from biotechnology. About 7.5%. A rising risk.
Technology, AI, or nanotechnology. About 5%. The uncertainty is very high.
Natural risks, asteroid or supervolcano. About 0.005%. Extremely unlikely in this window.
What these numbers are not
These are not facts. They are expert estimates.
Toby Ord estimates about a 16% existential risk this century. Others say about 19%. Others, much less.
The model assumes the risks are independent. In life, one makes another worse. Climate worsens, conflict rises, the chance of war rises with it.
Cooperation and technology can lower these numbers. It is not a prophecy. It is the range that today's knowledge allows.

About a 40% chance of some severe event at global scale by 2077. About 30% to 45% that Brazil faces serious crises. It is not inevitable. The chance it does not happen is higher than the chance it does.
